title: Capstone: Secure an API Estate
subtitle: OPA + Cedar + OpenFGA, tested and measured
content:
🎯 Mission

Secure a three-service payments API (public health, tenant-scoped reads, admin writes, per-document sharing) using at least two engines from this course: OPA/Rego for the API layer, Cedar for app rules, OpenFGA for document sharing. Ship policy + tests + measurements.

Time model (honest): 480 min across sessions — M1 policy (120) → M2 tests (120) → M3 enforcement (exactly one pattern) + evidence (240). Do not attempt in one sitting.

📦 Definition of Done

  • Rego bundle: default-deny, team/tenant rules, public carve-out; opa test green incl. cross-tenant deny + stranger deny + property tests.
  • Cedar: schema + permit/forbid set validating clean; owner/MFA/private semantics demonstrated.
  • OpenFGA: model with concentric viewer←editor + team indirection; tuple lifecycle (share/revoke) scripted; list-objects powering one listing endpoint.
  • Enforcement: one pattern from Lesson 19 running (sidecar/gateway/middleware) with fail-closed timeout config shown.
  • Evidence: decision-diff of one intentional rule change + p50/p99 PDP latency numbers + rollback + comms runbook.
  • Inference-risk note: one paragraph on what your controls do NOT stop (e.g. authorized-but-sensitive aggregation, allowed-tool composition) and what compensates.

📊 Rubric (14/20 to pass) — one artifact per row

Submit: repo layout (policies/, tests/, evidence/), opa test -v log, p50/p99 table, decision-diff file, rollback log. Score each row 0 (absent), partial (present but unchecked), or full (present and evidenced per the check). Points: partial = 1 pt on every row (including 2-pt row 7); full = listed pts. Max 20, pass at 14.

#Artifact (pts)PartialFull (3, or 2 for row 7)
1Default-deny + fail-closed config (3)Default set, timeout unconfiguredConfig shows default-deny + timeout=Xms AND a PDP-down → DENY test log line
2Deny/regression/property suite log (3)Allow-tests onlyopa test -v green with named cross-tenant, stranger, and garbage-input denies
3Two-engine seam tests (3)Two engines present, seams untestedRego tenant test AND FGA sharing test both green
4Share/revoke lifecycle transcript (3)Scripted but revoke untestedShare + revoke transcript AND cache-invalidation measurement shown
5p50/p99 latency table (3)Numbers without methodTable states n≥100, warm+cold split, tool named (e.g. hey/k6/opa bench), and fail-closed timeout for both percentiles
6Rollback log (3)Steps listed, never runLog with staging timestamps from a rehearsed rollback
7Decision-diff file (2)Diff shown, flips unjustifiedDiff file with every flipped verdict justified in one line each
🎮 Try it in the Policy Lab → Use the simulators to pre-validate each verdict before you build. Use the controls under the canvas to switch scenarios and watch the verdict change.

questions.question: Which engine answers 'which documents can anne view' for the listing endpoint?

options.text: OpenFGA list-objects (reverse query, not per-doc checks)
OPA opa eval in a loop over all ids
Cedar isAuthorized per document in a loop
None — listings skip authorization

questions.explanation: List-objects is the designed reverse query; per-doc check loops are N+1 authZ (Lesson 14).

questions.question: Minimum evidence your capstone must present?

options.text: Green tests (incl. denies) + latency p50/p99 + decision-diff + rollback steps
Decision logs alone without versioned policy
Passing allow-tests only, no deny-tests
The policy file alone

questions.explanation: The Definition of Done is evidence-shaped: tests, numbers, diffs, procedures — the audit triple from Lesson 5, integrated across engines.

questions.question: Sharing uses OpenFGA, reads use OPA. Where does tenant equality live?

options.text: In OPA policy (claim vs header), tested by the cross-tenant deny-test
Nowhere — OpenFGA implies tenancy
In the user's browser
Tenancy does not matter with sharing

questions.explanation: Each engine owns its seam: ReBAC the sharing graph, Rego the tenant invariant. Assuming one covers the other is the integration bug.

questions.question: Your PDP p99 is 40ms against a 10ms budget. First correct lever?

options.text: Fully-keyed short-TTL cache or embedded evaluation — measured, keeping fail-closed
Set failure_mode_allow: true
Remove the tenant check
Cache one ALLOW for everyone

questions.explanation: Latency fixes preserve the invariant: locality/caching keyed on the full decision inputs (Lessons 11, 19).

questions.question: A rule change accidentally allows strangers. What catches it before prod?

options.text: CI deny-tests + decision-diff preview showing the flipped verdicts
Nothing can catch it
The animation colors
Longer timeouts

questions.explanation: The Lesson 20 gates exist for exactly this: stranger-deny tests plus flip-previews on every policy PR.

questions.question: Cedar says Allow and OpenFGA says Deny for the same user action. Resolution?

options.text: Deny — seams combine deny-biased; investigate which seam owns the invariant
Allow — one yes outweighs one no
Average the two decisions
Ask the end user to decide

questions.explanation: Multi-engine estates deny on disagreement. Divergent engines mean a misplaced invariant — find which seam should own it.

questions.question: PDP p50 is 3ms and p99 is 400ms. Reading?

options.text: Tail dominated by cold starts or retries — warm, cache, or bound the slow path; report both
Fine — p50 is what users feel
Stop measuring p99
Raise the timeout to 30 seconds

questions.explanation: Averages hide the failures your users actually hit. Tail latency is the reliability budget.

questions.question: Your second engine adds no decision the first couldn't already make. Problem?

options.text: Integration theater — each engine must own a seam (API vs sharing vs app rules)
More engines are always better
No problem at all
Keep both — redundancy is always safer

questions.explanation: Engines multiply operational cost. Each must earn its place with decisions only it can make well.
